 Mfa No. 3695 of 2021
 Judgment

1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 24.06.2020 passed in MVC No.1603/2014 by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT-XV, Kunigal, (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein have Smt.Latha vs M.Vasantharaju on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88174763/
2 preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 04.10.2014 at about 6.10 p.m. the deceased Nagaraju B.N was traveling in a motor bike bearing registration No.KA-06-EA-9632 towards Bengaluru from Kunigal side, when he reached RMC yard, B.M. Road, another Motor bike bearing came from Bengaluru side in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor bike because of which,
the deceased Nagaraju B.N, fell down, at that time, a lorry bearing registration No.KA-21-B-8259 being driven in a rash and negligent manner went over Nagaraju B.N., because of which, he died.
The petitioners are the dependants of the deceased.

4. Based on the pleadings and the evidence let in, the Tribunal concluded that the accident happened due to rash and negligent riding of the lorry, which was duly insured with respondent No.2 and respondent No.2 is liable to pay of Rs.16,01,200/- to the petitioners along with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners have preferred this appeal.
5. Admittedly, the accident is of the year 2014.
The petitioners have failed to establish the income of the deceased before the Tribunal.
Hence, as per the chart prepared by the Lok-Adalath, the notional income to be taken for the year 2014 is Rs.8,500/- per month.
The deceased was aged about 33 years at the time of the accident.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121], a multiplier of '16' has to be adopted.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per the law down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v.
Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% needs to be added to his income.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co.Ltd. v.
Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Given the number of dependants, 1/4th of income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Thus, on the count of loss of dependency, petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.17,13,600/- (8,500 + 40% x 12 x 16 x 3/4).
6.

Further, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644], there are four dependants and they are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium(Rs.40,000x4= 1,60,000/-).

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Thus, in all, they are entitled to a sum of Rs. 19,03,600/- as against Rs.16,01,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.

7. Hence, the following:-
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
